title: SDK CI contracts + Phantom Env guide (draft)
content:
Quick note: this is a working sketch for a minimal, repeatable CI gating strategy aimed at reducing flaky SDK-to-platform integrations and shortening time-to-first-success for users. The core idea is to codify "contracts" (integration/telemetry/perf) and exercise them every PR using ephemeral "phantom" environments that emulate Redwood serving properties at a low fidelity but deterministic way.

Goals
- Prevent regressions that break common SDK flows (auth, streaming, retry semantics).
- Provide a fast local + CI harness that simulates the Redwood inference runtime for developer experimentation and for PR gating.
- Make contract tests easy to author and maintain by SDK teams (JS, Python, Go).
- Give clear failure signals and remediation steps so oncall / owners can triage quickly.

What problem this addresses
- Many SDK bugs surface only in integration with the hosted runtime (stream encoding, chunk ordering, manifest changes). PRs that change transports or telemetry often regress only at runtime.
- Running full infra/e2e is slow and brittle; we need a middle layer of deterministic, repeatable checks that catch 70–90% of regressions quickly before a full integration run.

Scope (what this doc covers)
- Definition of contract types and sample tests.
- Design for a phantom environment: what it must simulate and what it must not.
- CI wiring and lightweight local dev commands.
- Acceptance/exit criteria and rollout plan.
(Not covered: full-scale performance benchmarking against dedicated hardware; that's a separate pipeline.)

Definitions: contract types
- Integration contract: verifies core API shape, auth flows, request/response semantics (sync/generate, streaming, function call signals). Simple examples: send request with API key, expect 200 + JSON with tokens array, expect at-least-one stream-chunk header.
- Telemetry contract: ensures SDK emits expected telemetry events and attributes (request_id, model_name, latency_ms buckets). Test asserts event names and minimal attribute set.
- Performance contract (smoke): verifies SDK respects timeouts, backoff logic under simulated slow responses. These are cheap synthetic checks (e.g., 95th p95 < configured deadline) executed in phantom env.

Phantom environment: concept and minimal feature list
- Purpose: deterministic emulator that responds like Redwood runtime for typical happy- and common-edge paths. It runs in CI as a container and locally via docker-compose.
- Must simulate:
  - streamed chunk order and chunk boundaries (including occasional partial tokens)
  - kv-cache warm/empty responses (placeholder behavior)
  - latency injection (configurable deterministic delays)
  - error scenarios (429, 500, malformed JSON) for retry tests
  - telemetry sink (accepts telemetry POSTs so telemetry contract tests can assert payloads)
- Must NOT simulate: GPU-level performance characteristics, exact quantization outputs, or policy-level content moderation logic. Keep fidelity intentionally coarse.

Developer experience: local run steps (short)
- Prereqs: docker, make, node/python runtime.
- Start phantom env: make phantom-up  # boots emulator + telemetry sink (port 8081/8082)
- Run contract tests: make test-contracts-local  # runs pytest/mocha against phantom endpoint
- Tear down: make phantom-down
- If you need a more realistic run, there's a separate script to forward to staging runtime (controlled by flags and gating).

CI wiring (examples)
- Each SDK repo gets a new pipeline stage: contract-tests. Runs after unit tests, before release steps. Fail fast on contract failures.
- Example GitHub Actions (pseudo YAML):
  name: Contract Tests
  on: [pull_request]
  jobs:
    contracts:
      runs-on: ubuntu-latest
      steps:
        - uses: actions/checkout@v3
        - name: Start phantom env
          run: docker compose -f ci/phantom-compose.yml up -d --build
        - name: Run contracts
          run: npm run test:contracts || python -m pytest tests/contracts
        - name: Tear down
          run: docker compose -f ci/phantom-compose.yml down --volumes --remove-orphans
- Time budget: target < 4 minutes for contract stage on CI (aim to keep under 2 minutes). If a suite exceeds threshold, flag for splitting into faster smoke + slower sanity sets.

Sample test cases to include (starter matrix)
- Auth happy path: valid API key -> 200 + session header.
- Streaming ordering: three chunks arrive; SDK reassembles tokens in order.
- Partial-chunk handling: SDK must not drop partial token fragments between frames.
- Telemetry: SDK must POST event with {event: 'request.sent', sdk_version, model}.
- Retry/backoff: phantom returns 429 twice then 200; SDK retries per policy and surface a successful response.
- Error mapping: 500 must produce a specific SDK exception type (to avoid swallowing).

Data and artifacts we expect from a failing run
- Contract test logs (stdout captured).
- Phantom emulator logs and request/response traces (stored as artifact for 7 days).
- Minimal reproducible script: reproduce.sh that runs the failing test locally and collects logs. CI should upload these on failure.

Acceptance / Exit criteria for first rollout
- 90% of SDK repos have contract stage configured within 6 weeks of the initial roll.
- Contract failures block merges on main branches for SDK teams (opt-in grace window of 2 weeks per repo).
- Median contract test run time < 3 minutes.
- Sane failure signal: failure triage playbook reduces first-response time to an owner < 30 minutes (by piping to slack on-call).

Rollout plan (phases)
- Phase 0 (pilot): add to python-sdk and js-sdk repos only (2 weeks). Collect flaky tests and refine phantom behaviors.
- Phase 1: add to all client SDKs (polyglot) and create central template in github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-ci-templates.
- Phase 2: integrate telemetry contract consumer into /observability pipelines so alerts can be emitted when telemetry contract starts failing in downstream jobs.

Open questions / tradeoffs
- How deterministic should phantom be vs. realistic? More determinism = fewer flaky CI runs but may miss subtle issues.
- Where to host phantom images? Docker Hub vs internal registry (prefer internal registry due to private base images).
- Who owns long-term maintenance? Suggest SDK guild (rotating ownership) + one person from eng-platform as backup.

Short-term TODOs (next 2 weeks)
- [Maya] Push initial phantom prototype to github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-ci-templates (branch: phantom-proto).
- [Diego] Add three starter contract tests (auth, streaming ordering, telemetry) to python-sdk tests/contracts.
- [Aisha] Draft GH Action sample and a makefile snippet for local dev. Ticket: DEVEXP-472.
- [Samir] Add CI artifact upload on failures (logs + replay request body).

Notes / references
- Slack channel for discussion: #devexp-sdk (use this for quick triage).
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-ci-templates/pull/42
- Related Confluence draft: DEVEXP/SDK-CI-CONTRACTS

If you're reading this and want to help: pick one TODO above and drop a short comment in the PR or ping me (Maya) in slack. This is intentionally lightweight: the aim is to catch common regressions cheaply and make life easier for SDK authors and integrators.
